A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CompleteP research and contain 27 readable pages. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original transformer-training experiments on SlimPajama, downstream evaluations, hyperparameter analyses, and MNIST-based experiments on feature-learning dynamics.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the training comparisons, downstream scores, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Table 1 corrects embedding/unembedding AdamW epsilon for muP and alpha = 0.5 or 1 from epsilon_base to epsilon_base * m_N^-1; footnote 4 reports corresponding code fixes. This is a limited optimizer-prescription correction aligning the table with Equation (40), already present in v3.

E1.justification: Both versions use SlimPajama, the same six downstream benchmarks listed in Tables 2 and 6, and MNIST for the feature-learning experiment. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The reported comparisons retain SP, muP, and alpha = 0.5 alongside CompleteP, including the same appendix controls. The prescription correction is not accompanied by a newly evaluated comparator or revised comparison experiment.

E3.justification: Table 1, referenced by the experimental methodology, revises the reported embedding/unembedding epsilon setting to include inverse-width scaling. This corrects a stated setting without establishing that experiments were rerun. Budgets, model configurations, metrics, and other experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The coordinate checks, epsilon-scaling ablation, training-dynamics comparisons, weight-decay sweeps, and supplementary fitting analyses are retained with unchanged evidence in Figures 6–13.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains standard errors. Appendix G.4 retains 50 seeds per run and reporting of medians with first-to-third-quartile shading for Figure 6. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The figure graphics and empirical result tables are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains CompleteP's 11.8% and 34.4% FLOP savings for the optimal and deepest configurations, respectively; Table 3 also retains all validation losses.

T1.justification: Appendix D.4 corrects the weight-decay derivation's conclusion from lambda = Theta_{N,L}(1) to lambda = Theta_{N,L}(N), making it consistent with Table 1's existing width scaling. The main theoretical arguments and other derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about depth-wise hyperparameter transfer, complete feature learning, compute-efficient model shapes, and 12–34% compute savings.

C2.justification: The interpretations of depth-dependent performance and laziness remain unchanged, as do the limitations concerning fixed-token theory, three-point scaling-law fits, and architectural generalization in Section 7 and Appendix D.1.

D1.justification: New footnote 4 acknowledges table and official-code mistakes and reports fixes implementing the existing Equation (40) prescription. Equation (46) also replaces C with the defined FLOPs variable F, clarifying the batch-size formula without changing its coefficients or intended rule.

R1.justification: v4 adds Mlodozeniec et al., 'Completed hyperparameter transfer across modules, width, depth, batch and duration,' crediting it for identifying errors. Yang and Littwin's Tensor Programs IVb was already cited in v3 and is merely renumbered; the broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 adds a short correction footnote and makes local notation and citation edits. The section organization and substantive narrative remain essentially verbatim.

P2.justification: The corrected Table 1 entries and added footnote produce limited layout reflow across pages 4–7, including moving Findings 1 and 4 onto subsequent pages. No figure or table is added, removed, or redesigned.

improvement.justification: v4 resolves practical inconsistencies: Table 1 now agrees with the existing epsilon derivation, Appendix D.4 agrees with the weight-decay prescription, and Equation (46) uses the defined FLOPs variable. The code-fix disclosure improves transparency. These are useful, limited gains in correctness and reproducibility; the empirical evidence is unchanged, and no reruns are established.
